title: Sacred Earth, Shared Futures: Sustainability Education and Ecotheology Across Cultures
summary: We are living in an era of ecological urgency. Climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental degradation challenge not only our societies, but our values, beliefs, and ways of learning. This book responds by bringing together ecotheology and sustainability education in a global and interdisciplinary perspective. Emerging from the Akteo (Student Active Theology) collaboration between institutions in Norway, Madagascar, and Cameroon, this anthology explores how theological education can become a transformative force for ecological responsibility. Drawing on research and practice from both the Global North and South, it highlights the role of indigenous knowledge, liturgy, storytelling, and intercultural learning in shaping more sustainable ways of living. More than an academic anthology, Sacred Earth, Shared Futures: Sustainability Education and Ecotheology Across Cultures is a call to action. It invites educators, theologians, and students to engage deeply with the ecological crisis and to embrace a pedagogy rooted in hope, justice, and faith – pointing toward a more sustainable future for our shared Earth.
